concerns.text: Task T013 states: 'Validate file integrity via MD5/SHA checksums against known Planck values'. The Spec (FR-001) and Plan require validation against the Planck Legacy Archive's canonical checksums. The task description implies a hardcoded list of 'known values' which risks semantic weakening if those values are not dynamically fetched or explicitly cited as the canonical source, violating the 'Verified Accuracy' and 'Reproducibility' principles of the Constitution.

Task T015 implements the 2-pixel buffer zone as the PRIMARY method. The Spec Edge Cases explicitly mandate: 'Minkowski Functional computation uses a 2-pixel buffer zone... and applies Monte Carlo mask-corrected estimators'. The task description omits the mandatory 'Monte Carlo mask-corrected estimators' component, delivering only the buffer heuristic. This is a semantic weakening of FR-002/Edge Cases.

Tasks T024c and T025d define the verification metric for SC-002 (RMS deviation ≤1%). T024c compares against a 'theoretical genus curve' while T025d compares against a 'synthetic Gaussian map'. SC-002 explicitly requires measurement against the 'theoretical genus curve for a Gaussian field'. The task ambiguity creates a risk that the deliverable (T025d) will not satisfy the acceptance criterion (SC-002) if the synthetic map deviates from the theoretical curve, violating the 'No dropped acceptance criteria' rule.

Task T030b states: 'Abort if [runtime] exceeded'. FR-007 and SC-004 mandate that the system 'MUST complete the full analysis... within ≤6 hours'. A task that only detects failure and aborts does not satisfy the requirement to complete the analysis. This is a semantic weakening of the performance constraint, as the deliverable (an aborted run) fails the FR.

Phase 6 (T050-T054) introduces 'Frame Invariance' analysis and 'Physical Reality Check' metrics. The Spec (FR-001 to FR-007) and Plan define the scope strictly around data acquisition, MF computation, and statistical comparison against Gaussian/String hypotheses. There is no requirement for coordinate rotation or observer invariance testing. These tasks introduce unapproved scope (scope creep) that violates the 'No silent constitution drift' principle by adding paid-model-adjacent complexity (rotations) not demanded by the spec.

Task T035 describes performing a Likelihood Ratio Test using a 'Chi-squared distribution'. FR-005 and FR-006 explicitly require the test to 'account for covariance between functionals via sample covariance matrix'. A standard Chi-squared test assumes independence. The task description conflates the test statistic with the covariance handling, risking an implementation that ignores the multivariate correlation structure required by the Spec, thus failing FR-005.
